nodes.label: Config/Code Boundary
nodes.rationale: Thresholds and switches live in YAML; the rules that read them live in northfield/rules.py. A policy is a decision, a rule is a program, and pushing the program into YAML would mean inventing a worse language to write it in.

nodes.label: Escalate To Manager
nodes.rationale: Escalation names the reporting line rather than a person, so the policy survives a promotion.

nodes.label: End-of-Day Approval Deadline
nodes.rationale: An approval unanswered by end of day is re-examined: if the approver is away the next day it routes to their designated backup.

nodes.label: Enforce Part Qualification
nodes.rationale: A supplier must be both an approved vendor and qualified for the specific part. Enforced twice on the free-form path (gate rule, then the create tool) and structurally on the workflow path.

nodes.label: Material Shortfall Horizon (14 days)
nodes.rationale: A stand-in for multi-level MRP netting.

nodes.label: System Principal (system:harmony)
nodes.rationale: The non-human identity that runs detectors overnight and checks free/busy. Read and enqueue only - every change to a system of record traces to a named employee who approved it.

nodes.label: Profile Scope Intersection
nodes.rationale: Profile scopes are intersected with the users own entitlements, never added to them. Dana holds mail:send but this profile never asks for it, so her agent cannot send mail on her behalf even though she can.

nodes.label: Glob Tool Patterns
nodes.rationale: Glob patterns let a new ERP tool become available to a role without editing the profile; the gate and invoker still check scopes per call.

nodes.label: Scope-Denial Permission Boundary
nodes.rationale: Alex sees exactly the same shortfall Dana does and cannot act on it. The run reaches the gate, the gate denies the plan whole, nothing is written, and the audit names the rule and the missing scope - a real permission boundary rather than a staged one.

nodes.label: Free-Form Planning Path
nodes.rationale: workflows is empty: there is no declared workflow for a lot reallocation, so this agent runs the free-form path, keeping both paths exercised.

nodes.label: Profile-Only Extensibility
nodes.rationale: Adding this profile is the whole of what Scenario B required: no change to the orchestrator, the planner, the gate or the audit layer.

nodes.label: Purchasings Verbatim Requirement
nodes.rationale: We dont want the AI improvising a PO reroute. The steps are fixed... In that order. Every time. The planner decides whether to enter the workflow and supplies parameters; it cannot reorder, skip or add a step, and never sees this file.

nodes.label: Reversibility-Ordered Steps
nodes.rationale: Every compensable write comes before the one irreversible effect. Notify first, buy second would leave a supervisor acting on a PO that does not exist. Rollback safety is a property of the ordering, not only of the compensations.

nodes.label: Bounded Model Steps
nodes.rationale: choose_supplier looks like the model making a purchasing decision but is not: code computed who is qualified and removed anyone too slow. The model picks among options code produced. Neither model step may write - the loader rejects an llm step that names a tool.

nodes.label: on_empty: fail Confirmation
nodes.rationale: What makes step 1 a confirmation rather than a lookup: no qualified supplier means there is no reroute to make, and the workflow stops instead of proceeding to invent one.

nodes.label: enum_from Guardrail
nodes.rationale: Permitted answers are computed at run time from step 2 output. A supplier outside that list fails the guardrail, is audited as a rejection, retried once, then fails the workflow closed.

nodes.label: must_mention Guardrail
nodes.rationale: Forces the drafted message to name the production order and the new purchase order. A notification about a supply change that never says which one is not a notification.

nodes.label: Irreversible Step Declaration
nodes.rationale: irreversible: true rather than a missing compensation. The loader rejects a write that declares neither, so rollback is always a decision somebody made.

nodes.label: Step 5: Cancel Or Reduce Original PO
nodes.norm_label: step 5: cancel or reduce original po

nodes.label: Scopes As Permission Source Of Truth
nodes.rationale: Note what is absent as much as what is present: Priya cannot create purchase orders, and Alex cannot either - which is what makes the scope-denial failure case a real permission boundary.
nodes.norm_label: scopes as permission source of truth

nodes.label: Approved Vendor vs Part-Qualified
nodes.rationale: approved says this is a vendor Northfield does business with; approved_parts says which parts they are qualified to supply. They are different questions, and the difference is what the Apex Rapid Supply record exists to test.

nodes.label: The Apex Trap
nodes.rationale: An approved vendor, the cheapest price, next-day delivery, and an unsolicited email offering exactly the part Dana needs - but not qualified for P-4471. Two independent defences catch it: the approved-supplier workflow step never surfaces them, and the approved_supplier gate rule denies a plan that names them even if one is assembled by hand.

nodes.label: Days Of Cover (derived, never stored)
nodes.rationale: on_hand / daily_usage is the days of cover the shortfall detector computes; nothing here states it, because a stored derived value is a value that can be wrong.

nodes.label: Projection Beats Safety-Stock Alarming
nodes.rationale: P-3390 is below safety stock but PO-77801 arrives well before the order that needs it. A detector that alarmed on below-safety-stock would raise this; one that projects supply against demand does not.
